findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on all resources ("Resource": "*") to a long-lived IAM user. This violates least privilege and allows the user to read/modify all data in S3, launch or terminate any EC2 instance, and create or modify Lambda functions, which is a direct privilege-escalation and data-exfiltration path.

A permanent IAM access key is created for a human/service IAM user rather than using temporary credentials from an assumed role. The key never rotates, and its secret material is stored in Terraform state in plaintext (no pgp_key is set), so anyone with state access obtains credentials with the broad permissions granted by the attached policy.

The access key secret is exposed as a Terraform output and is not marked sensitive, so it will be printed to the console/CI logs on apply and stored readable in state, leaking credentials that carry wildcard ec2/s3/lambda/cloudwatch permissions.

Permissions are attached directly to a standalone IAM user with force_destroy enabled, bypassing group- and role-based access control and centralized credential lifecycle management; combined with the wildcard inline policy this creates a highly privileged static identity.
